finding.title: Server responses are slow across the site (median 2.22s)
finding.detail: Median time to first byte is 2.22s against a 0.8s target. TTFB is the floor for Largest Contentful Paint: no amount of front-end optimisation can produce a fast page on top of a slow server.
finding.fix: In order of typical payoff: enable full-page caching, put a CDN in front of the site, check for slow database queries on the main templates, and move off shared hosting if the host is the bottleneck.

finding.title: Pages are slow the first time they are requested (median 2.22s); repeated, 0.01s
finding.detail: Docket is the first visitor to most pages it reads, and the median first response was 2.22s against a 0.8s target. Asked again, the slowest pages answered in 0.01s: a cache in front of a slow server. Visitors who reach a page the cache already holds get it fast; the first visitor after it expires, and search engine crawlers working through pages nobody else has asked for lately, wait for the server.
finding.fix: Keep pages in the cache longer, warm it after publishing or clearing it, and speed up the origin itself: slow database queries on the main templates are the usual cause.

finding.title: Server response time is above target (median 1.13s)
finding.detail: Median TTFB 1.13s; Google's guidance is under 0.8s.
finding.fix: Add page caching and a CDN. This is usually a configuration change, not a rebuild.
